*thinking as the farmer...*

Aiya, another year starting. Forty years I've been working this little piece of ground — my hands know every corner of it. Just 1.5 mu, not much, but it's mine to manage. The children all grown, my son and his wife work in the county town now, they send money back for us old ones. Still, six mouths in the house when everyone comes back for holidays, and a little maize in the granary never hurts.

This year same as always — spring maize (春玉米). I don't do the wheat-maize double thing like some of the younger ones with bigger plots. At my age, one crop is plenty. Less rushing, less worry about that tight turnaround after wheat harvest. My back isn't what it used to be.

**Seeds** — I'll get the same hybrid I bought last year from Old Wang's shop in the village. Zhengdan 958, everyone plants it, my neighbor Li jiejie's field did well with it last year. About 30 yuan for enough seed for my 1.5 mu. I don't save seed from hybrid — that's a waste, grandson taught me.

**Planting** — End of April, beginning of May when the soil is warm enough. Not too early — one year I planted early and the cold nights hurt the seedlings, had to replant some spots. I learned. I'll ask my nephew to bring his small rotavator over to break up the field, give him some steamed buns and 80 yuan or so. Then plant by hand with my daughter-in-law when she comes home for the weekend, two of us can finish 1.5 mu in a day.

**Fertilizer** — One bag of compound fertilizer (复合肥, 15-15-15) per mu as base when I plant. That's how I've done it for years. Then when the maize is knee-high, about mid-July, I topdress with urea (尿素), maybe half a bag per mu — neighbor Zhang puts more, but urea is expensive and 1.5 mu doesn't need too much. If the leaves still look a bit pale I'll add a little more, but usually that's enough on my field. The soil here is decent, been working it for decades.

**Irrigation** — We have the village tube well. Maize is thirsty when it's tasseling and filling grain. I'll irrigate maybe 2 times — once after topdressing in July, once in August if no rain. Pumping costs money, around 40-50 yuan per mu each time, so I don't waste water. I watch the sky. If the summer rains come well, maybe only once.

**Pesticide** — I watch for armyworm (粘虫) and aphids. If I see them getting bad, I buy a small bottle of insecticide from Old Wang, spray once with the backpack sprayer. Usually once a year is enough, sometimes twice. My son bought me a little sprayer a few years ago, not heavy.

**Harvest** — Late September. My son comes back with his wife for a weekend to help, we pick the cobs by hand, dry them on the roof and in the yard. Eat some ourselves, sell the rest to the buyer who comes through the village with his truck.

I'm not trying to get the highest yield in the village — just a steady 400-450 kg per mu like always. That's enough. No need to spend extra on things I don't understand. My way has worked for forty years.
